faqs.q: Can you salary sacrifice a car on any hourly rate?
faqs.a: Salary sacrificing a car (via a novated lease) is generally available to employees of any pay level, but it depends on your employer offering the arrangement. The car lease payments come out of your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. However, the super guarantee is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, which may be reduced by salary sacrifice amounts. The calculator on this site does not include salary sacrifice, so you should seek professional advice for your specific situation.

faqs.q: How do the 2026–27 tax brackets affect my annual salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners. These brackets apply to your annual salary after any deductions or salary sacrifice.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Yes. The National Minimum Wage for casual employees includes a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. For example, from 1 July 2026 the base minimum is $26.44 per hour, and with casual loading it becomes $33.05 per hour. When converting to annual pay, you should use the loaded rate if you are a casual. The timesheet calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading to the base hourly rate you enter.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

If you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the basic formula to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This guide assumes a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. The fortnightly pay is simply the weekly amount multiplied by two.

Remember that this calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Many employees are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. These award rates vary by job type and experience. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details. If you are covered by an award, use that rate rather than the national minimum.

## Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the national minimum, that makes the casual rate $33.05 per hour. When you use the [timesheet](/) calculator, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator adds it for you. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this further.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax brackets are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Low-income earners may receive a reduction. The calculator on this site uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page shows how these deductions affect your net pay.

## Superannuation Guarantee Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee (SG) on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the SG rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super fund. The super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more information.

## Can You Salary Sacrifice a Car?

A common question is: **can you salary sacrifice a car**? Yes, if your employer offers a salary packaging arrangement, you can enter into a novated lease for a car. The lease payments and running costs are deducted from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. However, this also reduces your ordinary time earnings for super guarantee purposes, which may lower the super your employer pays. The calculator on this site does not include salary sacrifice, so your actual tax and super outcomes will differ. Always consult a tax professional or your employer’s salary packaging provider.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether to add casual loading. It then calculates your annual gross, weekly and fortnightly pay, estimated tax and Medicare, and superannuation. The results are based on the assumptions above. For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data). If you want to compare your pay to industry averages, the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page uses ABS data – note that these are averages, not medians for your specific job.

Remember, this is an estimate. For a precise determination of your pay, tax, and super, speak to your employer or a qualified accountant.
